The candidate must demonstrate the ability to transform an initial concept into a working, manufacturable product, with strong practical experience in mechanical design, CNC programming, electronics integration, embedded systems, and hardware assembly. Roles and Responsibilities 1. Product design and development - Translate business and technical requirements into complete hardware designs, specifications, and working prototypes. - Define product architecture, dimensions, materials, mechanisms, interfaces, and assembly methods. - Take ownership of development from concept through prototype validation and production handover. 2. Mechanical bodies and enclosures - Design equipment bodies, chassis, frames, cabinets, enclosures, mounting systems, and internal component layouts. - Produce detailed 3D models, manufacturing drawings, tolerances, and assembly drawings. - Address structural strength, vibration, heat dissipation, environmental protection, accessibility, and maintenance. - Select suitable materials and processes, including sheet metal fabrication, CNC machining, casting, molding, and additive manufacturing. 3. Robotics and electromechanical systems - Design and integrate robotic mechanisms, motion systems, actuators, motors, gearboxes, bearings, conveyors, and positioning assemblies. - Select and integrate sensors, encoders, limit switches, and control components. - Develop reliable mechanisms with appropriate accuracy, repeatability, load capacity, and safety features. 4. CNC programming and fabrication - Prepare CAD/CAM models, CNC toolpaths, and machining programs. - Define tooling, fixtures, cutting parameters, machining sequences, and inspection requirements. - Troubleshoot machining and fabrication issues and optimize production time, material use, and component quality. 5. Hardware assembly and testing - Personally support prototype assembly, wiring, mechanical fitting, calibration, and commissioning. - Develop assembly procedures, work instructions, test fixtures, and quality checkpoints. - Investigate failures, identify root causes, implement corrective actions, and verify improvements. 7. Manufacturing and supplier management - Prepare and maintain bills of materials, technical specifications, and manufacturing documentation. - Evaluate suppliers and fabrication workshops based on capability, quality, cost, and delivery. - Apply design-for-manufacturing and design-for-assembly principles. - Support pilot production and resolve issues before scaling production. 8.
